{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Lisa Ann Mantini''' is an American mathematician and educator.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url= https://www.maa.org/sites/default/files/Awards/MAAMathFest%202020_PrizesAwards_0.pdf|title=MAA Awards and Prizes|website=www.maa.org|pages=38|date=July 2020}}</ref> In 1995, while at Oklahoma State University, she received an MMA award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics.<ref name="2web" />

==Education==
Mantini earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] from the [[University of Pittsburgh]], and a [[Master of Arts]] and PhD from [[Harvard University]]. All these degrees were in mathematics.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.maa.org/news/mathematical-association-of-america-honors-members-with-service-awards|title=Mathematical Association of America Honors Members with Service Awards &#124; Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org|date=28 July 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/lisa-mantini |title=Lisa Mantini - Scholars &#124; Institute for Advanced Study |date=April 28, 2022 |website= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220428023304/https://www.ias.edu/scholars/lisa-mantini |archive-date=28 April 2022 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Teaching==
Mantini taught at [[Wellesley College]] prior to 1985. In 1985, she began to teach at [[Oklahoma State University System|Oklahoma State University]].<ref name="auto2"/> Among other awards (see below), in 1995 she received a [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics|Deborah and Franklin Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]],<ref name=2web>{{Cite web|url=https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award|title=Recipients of the Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics; Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240608175318/https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award |archive-date=8 June 2024 }}</ref> the highest teaching honor bestowed by the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref name="web">{{Cite web |url=https://www.maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/haimo-award-distinguished-teaching |title=Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award; Mathematical Association of America |website=www.maa.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220428021822/https://www.maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/haimo-award-distinguished-teaching |archive-date=28 April 2022 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://tsl.news/news2658/|title=HMC Professor Receives Haimo Award for Math Instruction|first=Tamara|last=Savage|date=November 9, 2012|website=The Student Life}}</ref> In 1998, she gave the undergraduate lecture course, "Representations of Finite Symmetry Groups", for the Mentoring Program for Women in Mathematics at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton, New Jersey.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ias.edu/math/wam/about/history |title=Program History - Women and Mathematics; Institute for Advanced Study |date=April 28, 2022 |website= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220428025543/https://www.ias.edu/math/wam/about/history |archive-date=28 April 2022 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Mathematical Association of America Governor==
Mantini served the Oklahoma-Arkansas Section of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] as Governor from 2002 to 2005 and from 2014 to 2017. This made her the first person to serve the Oklahoma-Arkansas Section of the Mathematical Association of America as Governor for two terms.<ref name="auto2"/>

==Notable publications== 
* An [[Integral transform|Integral Transform]] in L2-Cohomology for the Ladder Representations of U(p,q), J. Fun. Anal. 60, 211-242 (1985)
* An L2-Cohomology Construction of Negative Spin Mass Zero Equations for U(p,q), J. Math. Anal. Appl. 136, 419-449 (1988)
* An L2-Cohomology Construction of Unitary Highest Weight Modules for U(p,q), Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 323, 583-602 (1991)
* Inversion of an Integral Transform and Ladder Representations of U(1, q), in ''Representation Theory and Harmonic Analysis'', Contemp. Math. 191, AMS, Providence, 1995, pp.&nbsp;117–138 (with J. Lorch)
* To Challenge with Compassion: Goals for Mathematics Education, [[MAA FOCUS]] 15, Number 5 (October 1995), pp.&nbsp;10–11
* Power Series and Inversion of an Integral Transform, [[Pi Mu Epsilon|Pi Mu Epsilon Journal]] 10, 560-574 (1997) (with M. Oehrtman)
* [[Solomon Friedberg|Friedberg, Solomon]]. (2001). ''Teaching Mathematics in Colleges and Universities: Case Studies for Today's Classroom''. (Contributing author). United States: [[American Mathematical Society]]
* [https://math.okstate.edu/people/mantini/publications/carmona.pdf Intertwining Ladder Representations for SU(p,q) into Dolbeault Cohomology], in ''Non-Commutative Harmonic Analysis'', Progr. Math. 220, Birkhäuser, Boston, 2004, pp.&nbsp;395–418 (with J. Lorch and J. Novak)

==Notable recognition==
* 1994: Received the [[American Association of University Women|AAUW]]’s Founder’s Postdoctoral Fellowship<ref name="auto2"/>
* 1994: Was declared one of the Oklahoma-Arkansas Section of the [[Mathematical Association of America]]'s "Distinguished College/University Teachers of Mathematics" (one was chosen each year)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://sections.maa.org/okar/ |title=OK-AR MAA |date=April 28, 2022 |website= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220428021209/http://sections.maa.org/okar/ |archive-date=28 April 2022 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 1995: Received a [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics|Deborah and Franklin Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]],<ref name=web2>{{Cite web|url=https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award|title=Recipients of the Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics; Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240608175318/https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award |archive-date=8 June 2024 }}</ref> the highest teaching honor bestowed by the [[Mathematical Association of America]]<ref name="web"/><ref name="auto"/>
* 2020: Received a Certificate of Meritorious Service from the [[Mathematical Association of America]]<ref name="auto1"/>
